title: Invoice Data Extractor with Tesseract OCR and Excel Export
description:
A small command-line tool that reads a folder of invoices and receipts and writes one Excel sheet.

  • Images go through Tesseract OCR after a simple cleanup (grayscale, upscaling, contrast); PDFs with a text layer are read directly with pypdf.
  • Regular expressions find vendor, invoice number, invoice and due date, subtotal, tax, total and currency, in US and European number and date formats.
  • Plausibility checks flag missing fields, totals that do not add up and due dates before the invoice date.
  • The Excel file (openpyxl) has formatted dates and amounts, a filter, and highlights every row that needs a human check. CSV export is also available.
implementationSteps: Install Tesseract and the four pinned Python packages.
Collect the files of a folder: images (PNG, JPG, TIFF, BMP), PDFs and text files.
Read PDF text layers with pypdf; report PDFs without text instead of guessing.
Prepare images (grayscale, 2x upscale for small scans, autocontrast) and run Tesseract with --psm 6.
Apply regular expressions for invoice number, dates and labelled amounts; take the vendor from the first line.
Normalize dates (day-first by default, --us-dates for month-first) and amounts (1,234.56 and 1.234,56).
Check the result: required fields present, subtotal + tax = total, due date not before invoice date.
Write all rows to Excel with formats and highlight rows with problems; optionally write CSV.
Test the patterns on a sample of your own invoices and extend them where fields are missed.
performance:
Expectations, not measured results:

  • Clean, labelled invoices in English: number, date and total found in most cases; check on 20 to 50 of your own invoices.
  • Text files and text PDFs: milliseconds per file. Images: a few seconds per page for Tesseract, depending on size.
  • Every row with a missing or inconsistent field is marked, so errors are visible instead of silent.
userExperience: Run one command on a folder and open the Excel file: one row per document, dates and amounts already formatted, a filter on every column, and yellow rows with a short reason (for example "total not found") wherever someone should look at the original. The console prints a one-line summary per file.
